items.title: GitHub automation unavailable in this session: no pull request, no merge, no Pages deploy
items.detail: The GitHub CLI token in this environment is invalid and every api.github.com call returns HTTP 403 (rate-limited, unauthenticated). Workflow dispatch, PR creation, PR merge and the Pages deployment therefore could not be performed by this session. Commits were pushed to arena/f8feb803-olbg4 only. The site in this repository is complete and self-contained; publishing needs a working GitHub connection and one PR from this branch to main.

items.title: The requested band and the >70% rule leave a 1.43-point probability window; stronger picks cannot be published inside it
items.detail: At fair odds -250 is exactly a 71.43% implied probability. A pick that clears 70% but is stronger than 71.43% necessarily prices shorter than -250 and therefore falls outside the band the owner asked us to work in. 78 selections in this dataset clear 70% and price shorter than -250; they are published on the Strong picks page with their grade but without a prediction, because the brief restricts published high-confidence picks to the band. If the owner wants those in the published set, the band floor has to move (for example to -400) or the confidence rule has to change.

items.title: Published picks are concentrated in match totals
items.detail: Five of the seven published high-confidence picks are match totals and two are puck lines on alternate lines. That is a direct consequence of S-02: moneyline favourites on this card sit above 71.43% and fall outside the band, leaving the total and alternate-line markets as the only selections that land in the 70.00-71.43% window. It is a diversity limitation of the rule set, not a modelling preference.

items.title: NHL records were captured as of 21 October 9:25 PM EDT, after which at least one game finished
items.detail: The standings snapshot used for every rating is the NHL.com Wild Card table timestamped 'current as of Oct 21, 9:25 PM EDT'. The NHL.com schedule shows Florida losing 3-1 in Ottawa on 21 October, and the score feed for 22 October still lists Florida at 5-2-2. Team records, and therefore every rating built from them, may be one game stale for clubs that played late on 21 October. We did not adjust any record by hand.

items.title: No game-level backtest: the model's constants are declared, not fitted on this data
items.detail: The sandbox could not pull historical game logs (direct egress to league hosts is blocked and the refresh workflow needs Actions, which is unavailable), so the margin and total distributions are fixed at long-run league values and the shrinkage weights are policy choices. Accuracy, calibration and closing-line performance of this model are therefore unmeasured. Every constant is listed with its reason on the Methodology page.

items.title: MLB picks use regular-season records only; no pitcher adjustment was applied
items.detail: The World Series participants' final 2026 regular-season records, run differentials and last-ten records were read from the official MLB Stats API, but postseason results are not part of a regular-season standings table and were not modelled. A probable pitcher is published for Game 1 (Jacob Misiorowski, Milwaukee) and none for Games 2-5 at capture time, and no official ERA was captured, so no pitcher adjustment is applied anywhere. No MLB game reached the published high-confidence set.

items.title: Coverage: 14 in-scope sports were not captured in this session
items.detail: Three of the in-scope sports are covered in this build (ice hockey, baseball, snooker). The other in-scope sports are not captured: basketball, tennis, golf, cricket, rugby union, rugby league, handball, volleyball, table tennis, badminton, darts, esports and anything else outside the excluded list. They are absent because no official fixture page for 22-28 October 2026 could be read end to end from this sandbox in the time available, not because they were judged out of scope. Nothing is listed for them, rather than listed with invented values.

items.title: Venue blank on 15 of 31 NHL rows
items.detail: Venue was recorded only where the official NHL score feed for that date published it. For the other rows the cell is blank rather than filled from an unofficial source. Each row still carries its official GameCenter link, which states the venue.

items.title: Four published picks sit on alternate lines (4.5, 7.5, +2.5)
items.detail: Standard NHL totals are 5.5 or 6.5 and the standard puck line is 1.5. Where no selection on a standard line landed inside the requested band, the pick is quoted on an alternate line and labelled as such on the card and in the table.

items.title: OLBG.com itself could not be crawled from this environment
items.detail: Direct requests to olbg.com fail from the build sandbox (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, egress allowlist). The fixture universe in this desk therefore comes from the official league pages, not from an OLBG crawl, and no OLBG event id is claimed. The OLBG taxonomy used to decide which sports are in scope is the one recorded by earlier sessions in data/olbg-taxonomy.json.

items.title: Start times are published in ET exactly as NHL.com prints them, not converted
items.detail: Converting Eastern times to UTC would introduce an inference (and DST questions) that the source page does not make, so the table prints the published local time and labels the column 'ET, as published'. MLB start times are the UTC values returned by the official API.

items.title: One published pick rests on a seven-game sample
items.detail: The Los Angeles Kings have played seven games and the pick on their +2.5 puck line uses that sample. The high-confidence gate requires seven games; it is the weakest sample in the published set. The Carolina, Nashville and Colorado picks rest on 8-11 games.

items.title: The rest of the repository was not re-audited line by line in this session
items.detail: The repository carries a 317-row master board and a dozen earlier dashboards, all cut off on 21 October. They were left byte-identical. This session's verification register covers its own 36 rows and 7 predictions; it does not re-open the earlier boards, whose own registers, flags and sources remain the authority for their rows. Readers should treat those pages as dated snapshots.

items.title: Snooker match format is recorded from observed frame scores, not a printed format line
items.detail: Every completed match on the official WST matches page for the BetVictor Northern Ireland Open 2026 (rounds 1-2, 18-21 October) ends with the winner on exactly four frames (4-0, 4-1, 4-2 or 4-3), which is why the eight Round 3 matches are priced as first to four / best of seven. The page itself does not print a 'best of seven' line, so the format is an observation from the official frame scores rather than a quoted rule. If a later round changes format, the frame handicap and total-frames prices on that round would be wrong.

items.title: Six earlier high-confidence write-ups were retired when the standings snapshot was re-read
items.detail: The first standings snapshot of this session produced seven in-band high-confidence picks. Re-reading the official NHL wildcard standings into desk/data/nhl_standings.json moved six of them outside the 70.00%-71.43% publishable window, so their write-ups moved to desk/data/retired_predictions.json rather than being deleted or left attached to picks that no longer exist. Five picks remain published (three NHL, two snooker) and every one has a hand-written prediction.

items.title: One snooker match is priced on a 50/50 baseline because no player statistics could be captured
items.detail: Jordan Brown v Scott Donaldson (Round 3, 15:00, 22 October 2026) is listed on the official WST matches page but the Match Centre season statistics for both players were not captured before this build. The row therefore carries blank inputs, a 50/50 baseline, no High grade and an explicit flag; no value was inferred for either player.
